verdict.rationale: First-party interpreter docs state that Python, JavaScript and TypeScript code can be executed with rich outputs, including charts, tables, data visualizations and formatted data. Contexts keep state across executions, and the last expression is returned automatically (pandas example). Beyond the interpreter, exec() runs arbitrary shell commands in a full Linux container, so other runtimes are reachable that way. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration that rich outputs (charts, tables) work as claimed, and first-class interpreter support for languages beyond Python/JS/TS.
